newsitem.title: UK: Britain's Heseltine says EMU may be delayed.
newsitem.headline: Britain's Heseltine says EMU may be delayed.

text.p: Britain's deputy prime minister Michael Heseltine said it was possible that European monetary union might be delayed beyond the planned start date of January 1, 1999.
"The circumstances that are now increasingly obvious make it very possible that the whole process itself might be subject to delay -- we don't know," he told ITN television.
Heseltine was being asked about a comment on Sunday by Health Secretary Stephen Dorrell that Britain would not join a single currency in the first wave in 1999. Dorrell later withdrew the comment.

Heseltine said Britain had the option to negotiate and to decide on the basis of its national self-interest whether or not to join a single currency. "When we know the facts we will then decide," he said.

He dismissed suggestions that conflicting comments from cabinet members on monetary union reflected a jockeying for position in the race to succeed Prime Minister John Major as Conservative party leader if he loses the forthcoming election.
"I don't agree with that. I know these colleagues very well and I believe they are absolutely determined to secure the re-election of John Major and the Conservative government," Heseltine added.
